description: Count to ten with a little fish at the seaside! Sing 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Once I Caught a Fish Alive with Robo: a fish jumps out of the sea, splash! We count to five and then to ten on our fingers while bubbles float up out of the water and the ten-bubble tracker fills. The fish hops into Robo's soft net to say hello, and then we let it go again and wave bye-bye. It swims home to Mummy Fish and Baby Fish. Then play the which-way game: the fish swims to the left or to the right, point and count 3, 2, 1! A gentle ending: no one gets hurt, and the fish swims home.

youtube.description:
Count to ten with a little fish at the seaside! Sing 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Once I Caught a Fish Alive with Robo: a fish jumps out of the sea, splash! We count to five and then to ten on our fingers while bubbles float up out of the water and the ten-bubble tracker fills. The fish hops into Robo's soft net to say hello, and then we let it go again and wave bye-bye. It swims home to Mummy Fish and Baby Fish. Then play the which-way game: the fish swims to the left or to the right, point and count 3, 2, 1! A gentle ending: no one gets hurt, and the fish swims home.

What your child learns: counting from 1 to 10 on their fingers (to five on one hand, to ten on two), the numbers in order, and left and right.

Sing at home: hold up a finger for each number, wiggle your hand like a fish, and when the fish swims away, point and say "left!" or "right!" together. Then wave bye-bye as you let your pretend fish go. The first four lines are the traditional public-domain rhyme; the gentle ending (the fish swims home, to the left and to the right) is original, written for Toy Box Friends in place of the old finger-biting lines.

Made for kids. Toy Box Friends: 3D learning videos for babies, toddlers and preschool.
